oracle: The r4-v2b-record.json envelope delta (gpttmpl.* facts), produced by the windows-console-driver R4 observer gpo_observers/gpttmpl_inf.py, controller-side and independent of the actuation path and of gpo_studio.security_template. The SYSVOL file itself was not retained; the encoding facts, section list, and the three registry-key rows below are the banked measurement.
transcript_format: ASCII rendering of the captured UTF-16LE file: a two-line measurement header (first 4 bytes, CR/LF counts, total byte size), then the decoded content verbatim except that each CRLF was transcribed as LF. Unlike the scripts.ini captures there is NO leading blank line: the first native character is the '[' of [Unicode], so the content starts immediately after the header. The banked counts pin the framing exactly: 3 section headers + 1 + 2 + 3 banked content lines = 9 CRLF-terminated lines, so the file has no blank lines, no comments, and a CRLF terminator on the last line. The total byte size is computed from the reconstruction, not banked by the record. Two choices the record does not pin: the text of the three key=value lines in [Unicode]/[Version] (only per-section line counts and key_value_shape=true are banked) -- the canonical GPMC values Unicode=yes, signature="$CHICAGO$", Revision=1 are used -- and tight '=' spacing. The [Registry Keys] row order IS banked (reverse of authoring order: Charlie, Bravo, Alpha), as are the rows verbatim.
native_byte_reconstruction: b'\xff\xfe' + transcript_content.replace('\n', '\r\n').encode('utf-16-le'); tests re-verify CR count, LF count, crlf_only and total length against the banked values
related_measurement: The same record shows GPMC registering the SecEdit extension pair {827D319E-6EAC-11D2-A4EA-00C04F79F83A}{803E14A0-B4FB-11D0-A0D0-00A0C90F574B} in gPCMachineExtensionNames and laying down Machine/Microsoft/Windows NT/SecEdit/GptTmpl.inf. Propagation codes are distinct per authored key: Alpha=0, Bravo=2, Charlie=1 (the mapping the R4 capture was run to settle). Feeding the reconstruction to gpo_studio's parse_security_template yields 3 unknown_lines -- the committed number for the first native template ever parsed, input to WI-038.
sanitisation: Verified against the banked record before copying: the rows contain only synthetic zzStudio* placeholder key names and well-known principals (BA, CO, SY, BU) plus the well-known capability SID S-1-15-2-1, which is a Windows constant, not an estate identifier. No domain, host, account, e-mail, or user-path identifiers.
